name: BEEGND-1
description:
### Station BEEGND-1

**B**erlin **E**xperimental and **E**ducational **G**rou**nd** Stations (**BEEGND**) are a series of stations built as part of a teaching project at [Technische Universität Berlin (TUB)](https://www.tu.berlin/).

BEEGND-1 is a fixed-antenna station in a remote, low-noise location (Hoher Fläming) about 80 km Southwest of Berlin. It comprises of two fixed-direction UHF Turnstile Antennas, SAW-Filters and a custom built [LNA-Filter-Board](https://git.dk0tu.de/afutub/famp-pcb/-/tree/rev3) and an Ettus B210-mini SDR.

The station enables observations in the UHF-Amateur (~435MHz) and in the UHF-Commercial (~400MHz) Band. It was build as part of TUBs [BEECON-Project](https://www.tu.berlin/en/raumfahrttechnik/research/current-projects/beecon), which develops a standardised satellite identification and tracking solution to improve Space Situational Awareness.

#### Quick Notes on Operations

Please mind some short remarks on the stations operation:

- The station uses fixed turnstile antennas. Thus, low-elevation passes will most certainly not perform well. The antennas work best at an elevation above 20 to 25 degrees.
- The station provides IQ-Data automatically. These can be loaded from: [https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/DkiRJ9jyLKRBmXE](https://tubcloud.tu-berlin.de/s/DkiRJ9jyLKRBmXE). The IQ-Data comes directly from the satnogs-flowgraph. It is doppler-corrected by the observations TLE. Please mind, that we will keep the data only for a limited time due to memory constraints.
- On this station we run a patched satnogs-client. It supports using both antenna ports of the Ettus SDR and chooses the right port based on the frequency requested in the observation

We are looking forward to see good observations. :)
